steps.title: Count failed, unknown-account and successful logins
steps.do: At the prompt type grep -c "Failed password" auth-jump01.log while speaking, with no pause, then press Return. Rest the cursor on the 53 in the output. On the next prompt type grep -c "invalid user" auth-jump01.log while speaking, with no pause, then press Return. Slide the cursor down onto the 14 in the output. Move the cursor between the 53 and the 14: these are the bar the pivot has to hit, and if the pivot is not 53, a row went astray. On the next prompt type grep 'Accepted' auth-jump01.log (Accepted in single quotes) while speaking, with no pause, then press Return. Sweep the cursor down the six Accepted lines: three publickey, three password. Rest the cursor on the second line, the 03:52:34 line, Accepted password for svc_backup, and say you will come back to it. Rest the cursor on the password lines and say an IP that failed and then got in needs its account checked, so those IPs are compared in the sheet first.

steps.title: Build the pivot table

steps.do: Move down to cell A1 and click it. Pause 1 s after "I'll click it". Press Command A while speaking, with no pause, and read the name box at the top left: A1:G60. Move up to Insert in the menu bar and open it. Pause 1 s after "I open it". Move down the Insert list to Pivot table and choose it. Pause 1 s after "I'll choose it". In the Create pivot table box pick New sheet. Pause 1 s after "I'll pick it". Click Create at the bottom right of the box with a left click. Pause 1 s after "a left click". Slide the cursor along the bottom tabs onto Pivot Table 1, then up to the editor open on the right. Think aloud: one formula per pair is a lot of typing and a pivot counts them all at once, so the pivot. In the editor click Add beside Rows. Pause 1 s after "I'll click it". In the list that drops down move to src_ip and click it. Pause 1 s after "click it". Move further down to Columns and click its Add button with a left click. Pause 1 s after "a left click". From the list select event. Pause 1 s after "select it". Lower on the Columns card untick Show totals. Pause 1 s after "I'll untick Show totals". Slide the cursor along the pivot's header row from left to right: Accepted password, Accepted publickey, Failed password. Move down to Values and click its Add button. Pause 1 s after "I'll click it". In the list pick event. Pause 1 s after "pick event". Look lower on the value card at the Summarize by box to see what it is set to. If it already reads COUNTA, leave it and say so. Only if it reads SUM: open that dropdown, move down to COUNTA and pick it. Pause 1 s after "COUNTA and pick it". Say that each log line is one attempt, so COUNTA fits. Slide the cursor down the pivot to the Grand Total row at the bottom as the counts fill in.

steps.title: Last look, check and epilogue
steps.window: Google Sheets: Pivot Table 1 still on screen, Dock on the left
steps.do: The pivot is still on screen. Slide the cursor down the address column, then across to the Decision column: six addresses ranked, a decision beside each. Run the cursor down the Failed password column, then across each row to its Decision cell: Block beside 18 and 14, Watch beside 9 and 7, Ignore beside 3 and 2; the six add up to 53, the same as Terminal. Then say the closing paragraph as one single block, moving the cursor on the pivot as the spoken words reach each figure: the Decision column and the Grand Total, the 53; the bottom tabs; the Data menu; the header row; the first address row and its 18 and the 14; the Block pair; the Watch pair with their 9 and 7; the Ignore pair with their 3 and 2; the whole table from its top-left cell to the last Decision cell; the File menu; the two Watch rows; the header row again; then the Decision cells for Block 2, Watch 2 and Ignore 2. At the end slide left off the grid and rest on the Dock at the left edge until the paragraph ends.
say: "Step 18: the pivot's still on screen, so that's the final look. The six addresses are ranked down the left, with a decision beside each."
"Checking the verdicts against the counts: Block beside 18 and 14, Watch beside 9 and 7, Ignore beside 3 and 2. Those six add up to 53, same as Terminal."

"So, start to finish. I began in Terminal and counted the log: 59 lines, 53 of them Failed password, and 14 of those on accounts that don't exist, so I had numbers to check against later. Then I went to the sheet with the log data and checked all 59 rows were there. I froze the header, added a filter from the Data menu, and built a pivot of source address against event type, and its failure total came to 53, the same as Terminal, so I trusted it. After that I went down the ranking. I filtered the top two addresses to their rows and read the users and times, read the other four straight off the pivot, and typed a verdict beside each one. The Block pair is the two biggest piles, 18 failures and 14, both from outside, with no login at all, and one of them only ever tried accounts that don't exist. That fits my rule: an outside address with five or more failures and no login gets blocked for 24 hours. The Watch pair failed 9 times and 7 times and then got in, one as svc_backup and one as jsmith. I didn't block them, because a block could lock out a real person, and a guessed password could still be live. So they get an account action instead: a password reset for svc_backup, and a check with jsmith. The Ignore pair is the internal admin, who failed three times and then logged in, with publickey logins either side, and one outside address with just 2 tries, under five and no login, which is noise. Neither of those needs a block. I copied the table into the note, wrote the action lines for the firewall owner, and downloaded the note and the sheet. Both landed in the browser's downloads. The hard part was telling Watch from Block when an address failed and then got in, because I couldn't tell a guess from the real user. Next time I'd check each address's Accepted lines before building the pivot. So, for the goal: before the morning standup, last night's failed logins on jump01 are sorted. Block 2, Watch 2, Ignore 2, and the note tells the firewall owner what to act on, what to watch, and what to leave alone."
